```{r auc_bridge, eval = isTRUE(params$auc_bridge)}
    r <- roc(mb$lab_geneset, mb$pred, direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
    ci <- as.numeric(ci.auc(r))
    matched_auc <- as.numeric(auc(r))
    cat(sprintf("Matched-gene AUC (held out by both models): %.4f [95%% CI %.3f-%.3f], n = %d - underpowered by design\n",
                matched_auc, ci[1], ci[3], nrow(mb)))
  }
} else {
  cat("\nNOTE: 02_'s rf_model_data not found; overlap and matched-gene AUC skipped\n")
}
```

# Importance

Reports which features the forest relied on, and plots the fit.

**Decisions**

- Report impurity importance here, and treat family-level sums as descriptive only. Impurity is
  not additive, so summing it within a family is not exact. `11_shap_regression.Rmd` gives the
  exact split using SHAP.


```{r importance}
importance_df <- tibble(
  feature    = names(rf_model$variable.importance),
  importance = as.numeric(rf_model$variable.importance)
) %>%
  left_join(annotation %>% dplyr::select(feature, family, block), by = "feature") %>%
  arrange(desc(importance)) %>%
  mutate(share_pct = 100 * importance / sum(importance), rank = row_number())
print(as.data.frame(head(importance_df, 20)), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nFamily shares (impurity is NOT additive - descriptive only; 11_ gives the exact SHAP split):\n")
print(as.data.frame(importance_df %>% group_by(family) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), share_pct = round(sum(share_pct), 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(share_pct))), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r fig_fit, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.6, eval = isTRUE(params$auc_bridge)}
# Predicted vs observed on held-out genes, and the same separation the AUC bridge summarises.
# Gated on `auc_bridge` because panel (b) reads `br` and `bridge`, which exist only if the
# auc_bridge chunk above ran. Without the gate a run with auc_bridge = FALSE dies here with
# "object 'br' not found" - an infrastructure crash that a mutation test would misread as a
# check having fired.
p_fit <- tibble(obs = test_data$y, pred = pred_t) %>%
  ggplot(aes(obs, pred)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.18, size = 0.7, colour = "#E69F00") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.5,
           label = sprintf("Spearman = %.3f\nPearson = %.3f\nn = %d",
                           spearman_raw, pearson_raw, nrow(test_data))) +
  # Derived, not typed. .dir_ratio is built from params in the direction_facts chunk; hardcoding
  # "si3d" here put the wrong knockdown on every si3e figure, and the sibling legend below put
  # the wrong CONDITION on the normoxia figure. Same failure as the directional prose: a label
  # that does not come from the data will eventually disagree with it.
  labs(x = paste0("observed TE LFC, ", .dir_ratio), y = "predicted",
       title = "(a) Held-out fit",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d features | transform: %s", length(feature_cols),
                          params$target_transform)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)

# The legend name for the positive class, built from params rather than written out. CLAUDE.md's
# group_colors block uses the literal "eIF3d hypoxia promotes"; copying that string verbatim is
# what put "hypoxia" on the normoxia figure.
pos_label_txt <- sprintf("%s %s %s", .dir_gene, params$condition, params$direction)
p_sep <- br %>% filter(!is.na(lab_geneset)) %>%
  mutate(cls = if_else(lab_geneset == 1, pos_label_txt, "Negative control")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(pred, fill = cls, colour = cls)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(c("#E69F00", "black"),
                                      c(pos_label_txt, "Negative control")), name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c("#E69F00", "black"),
                                        c(pos_label_txt, "Negative control")), name = NULL) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.4,
           label = sprintf("bridge AUC = %.3f\nceiling = %.3f\nn = %d / %d",
                           bridge$auc[1], bridge$ceiling[1], bridge$n_pos[1], bridge$n_neg[1])) +
  labs(x = "predicted TE LFC", y = "density", title = "(b) AUC bridge",
       subtitle = "the regression never saw these labels") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.5, 0.96))

pg <- cowplot::plot_grid(p_fit, p_sep, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 1.15))
print(pg)
ggsave_if(here("plots", paste0("10_fit_", suffix, ".pdf")), pg, width = 10, height = 4.6)
```

# Comparison with the classifier

Four views of how this regression relates to `02_rf_model.Rmd`'s classifier. Everything here
reads saved artifacts and refits nothing, and each part skips cleanly if its inputs are absent.

This is the summary view. `12_regression_vs_classifier.Rmd` carries the full treatment, including
the measured noise floor that decides which differences are real.

**Decisions**

- Compare the classifier's predictions only on genes it never trained on. It modelled 2,872 of
  the 10,172, so most of this notebook's held-out set is genuinely unseen by it.
- Compare importance and SHAP as shares, never as raw values. The two models' SHAP is in
  different units.
- Plot the shrinkage explicitly, since it is the main thing that makes the held-out fit above
  look worse than the ranking actually is.

```{r fig_roc_and_calibration, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.6, eval = isTRUE(params$auc_bridge)}
# Gated on `auc_bridge` for the same reason as fig_fit: panel (a) is built from `br`, which the
# auc_bridge chunk creates. Panel (b) needs only `pred_t`, but the two panels share one
# cowplot grid, so the chunk is gated as a unit.
#
# (a) The bridge as an ROC curve rather than two densities, with the ceiling curve drawn. The
# ceiling uses the true outcome as the predictor: for a label that is a threshold on that
# outcome it is perfect by construction, which is why the AUC is never reported on its own.
roc_geneset <- roc(br$lab_geneset[!is.na(br$lab_geneset)],
                   br$pred[!is.na(br$lab_geneset)], direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
roc_ceiling <- roc(br$lab_geneset[!is.na(br$lab_geneset)],
                   br$y[!is.na(br$lab_geneset)], direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
roc_thresh  <- roc(br$lab_thresh, br$pred, direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)

roc_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(fpr = 1 - roc_geneset$specificities, tpr = roc_geneset$sensitivities,
         curve = sprintf("predicted TE vs classifier gene sets (AUC %.3f)",
                         as.numeric(auc(roc_geneset)))),
  tibble(fpr = 1 - roc_thresh$specificities, tpr = roc_thresh$sensitivities,
         curve = sprintf("predicted TE vs a threshold on the outcome (AUC %.3f)",
                         as.numeric(auc(roc_thresh)))),
  tibble(fpr = 1 - roc_ceiling$specificities, tpr = roc_ceiling$sensitivities,
         curve = sprintf("ceiling: TRUE outcome as the predictor (AUC %.3f)",
                         as.numeric(auc(roc_ceiling)))))

p_roc <- ggplot(roc_df, aes(fpr, tpr, colour = curve)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_path(linewidth = 0.9) + coord_equal() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#E69F00", "#0072B2", "grey45"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "false positive rate", y = "true positive rate", title = "(a) The AUC bridge as a ROC",
       subtitle = sprintf("held-out genes only | n = %d positives, %d negatives",
                          sum(br$lab_geneset == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
                          sum(br$lab_geneset == 0, na.rm = TRUE))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.98, 0.02), legend.justification = c(1, 0),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5))

# (b) Why the held-out fit looks flat. A forest prediction is an average over leaf values, so
# predictions shrink toward the training mean. Binning the held-out genes by predicted value and
# plotting the mean observed value in each bin shows the ranking is monotone even though the
# magnitudes are compressed.
calib <- tibble(pred = pred_t, obs = test_data$y) %>%
  mutate(bin = ntile(pred, 10)) %>% group_by(bin) %>%
  summarise(pred_mid = mean(pred), obs_mean = mean(obs), obs_se = sd(obs) / sqrt(n()),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop")
sd_ratio <- sd(pred_t) / sd(test_data$y)
p_cal <- ggplot(calib, aes(pred_mid, obs_mean)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = obs_mean - obs_se, ymax = obs_mean + obs_se),
                width = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, colour = "#E69F00") +
  geom_line(colour = "#E69F00", linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.08, vjust = 1.3,
           label = sprintf("prediction sd / outcome sd = %.3f\n(predictions compressed %.1fx)\nn = %d in 10 bins",
                           sd_ratio, 1 / sd_ratio, nrow(test_data))) +
  labs(x = "mean predicted TE LFC in bin", y = "mean observed TE LFC in bin",
       title = "(b) Ranking is monotone; magnitudes are shrunk",
       subtitle = "decile bins of held-out genes. Dashed line is y = x") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)

pg_roc <- cowplot::plot_grid(p_roc, p_cal, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1.1, 1))
print(pg_roc)
ggsave_if(here("plots", paste0("10_roc_calibration_", suffix, ".pdf")), pg_roc,
          width = 11, height = 4.6)
```

```{r fig_vs_classifier, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.8}
clf_model_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("rf_classifier_", clf_suffix, ".rds"))
clf_md_path2   <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("rf_model_data_", clf_suffix, ".rds"))
clf_imp_path2  <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("rf_importance_", clf_suffix, ".csv"))
have_clf <- all(file.exists(c(clf_model_path, clf_md_path2, clf_imp_path2)))

if (!have_clf) {
  cat("Classifier artifacts not found; this comparison needs 02_rf_model.Rmd to have been knit.\n")
} else {
  clf      <- readRDS(clf_model_path)
  clf_md2  <- readRDS(clf_md_path2)
  # The classifier can only score these genes if it was fitted on the same columns in the same
  # order, so that is checked - but a mismatch is a MISSING INPUT for this comparison, not a
  # corrupt run, and the section header promises each part skips cleanly when its inputs are
  # absent. It was a stopifnot, which aborted the whole render: that made every arm that
  # deliberately changes the feature set unrunnable, including family_arms_reg()'s `none` arm
  # (exclude_families drops 9 columns for g4, 5 for peptide) and so both family presets.
  # Reported rather than silently dropped, because an UNintended mismatch looks the same.
  same_features <- identical(clf_md2$feature_cols, feature_cols)
}
if (have_clf && !same_features) {
  cat(sprintf(paste0("Panels (c) and (d) SKIPPED: the classifier was fitted on %d features and ",
                     "this run uses %d, so it cannot score these genes.\n"),
              length(clf_md2$feature_cols), length(feature_cols)))
  only_clf <- setdiff(clf_md2$feature_cols, feature_cols)
  only_reg <- setdiff(feature_cols, clf_md2$feature_cols)
  if (length(only_clf)) cat("  only the classifier has:", paste(only_clf, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  if (length(only_reg)) cat("  only this run has:      ", paste(only_reg, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  if (!length(only_clf) && !length(only_reg))
    cat("  the same columns in a DIFFERENT ORDER, which is a different forest\n")
  cat("  Expected when the arm excludes a family; investigate if it was not meant to.\n")
}
if (have_clf && same_features) {
  # Only genes the classifier never trained on. It modelled 2,872 of 10,172, so most of this
  # notebook's held-out set is unseen by it and the comparison is out-of-sample on both sides.
  unseen <- !(test_data$gene_id_clean %in% clf_md2$train$gene_id_clean)
  clf_p  <- predict(clf, test_data[unseen, feature_cols])$predictions[, clf_md2$pos_label]
  cmp_df <- tibble(reg_pred = pred_t[unseen], clf_prob = clf_p,
                   obs = test_data$y[unseen],
                   in_pos = test_data$gene_id_clean[unseen] %in% pos_genes)
  rho_pred <- cor(cmp_df$reg_pred, cmp_df$clf_prob, method = "spearman")

  p_pp <- ggplot(cmp_df, aes(clf_prob, reg_pred)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = in_pos), size = 0.8, alpha = 0.35) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#E69F00", `FALSE` = "grey55"),
                        labels = c(`TRUE` = "in the positive set", `FALSE` = "not"), name = NULL) +
    annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.08, vjust = 1.3,
             label = sprintf("Spearman = %.3f\nn = %d genes\nneither model trained on these",
                             rho_pred, nrow(cmp_df))) +
    labs(x = "classifier predicted probability", y = "regression predicted TE LFC",
         title = "(c) Do the two models order genes the same way?",
         subtitle = "genes held out by this model and never seen by the classifier") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

  # (d) Impurity importance as shares. Shares rather than raw values, because the two forests
  # split on different quantities and their raw impurity is not on one scale.
  clf_imp2 <- read_csv(clf_imp_path2, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(clf_share = 100 * importance / sum(importance)) %>%
    dplyr::select(feature, family, clf_share)
  imp_cmp <- importance_df %>% dplyr::select(feature, reg_share = share_pct) %>%
    inner_join(clf_imp2, by = "feature")
  rho_imp <- cor(imp_cmp$clf_share, imp_cmp$reg_share, method = "spearman")

  p_imp <- ggplot(imp_cmp, aes(clf_share, reg_share)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
    geom_point(aes(colour = family), size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(guide = "none", end = 0.9) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = imp_cmp %>% filter(pmax(clf_share, reg_share) > 2.5 |
                                abs(clf_share - reg_share) > 1.5),
      aes(label = feature), size = 2.5, max.overlaps = 18, seed = 9) +
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.5,
             label = sprintf("Spearman = %.3f\nn = %d features", rho_imp, nrow(imp_cmp))) +
    labs(x = "classifier impurity share (%)", y = "regression impurity share (%)",
         title = "(d) Feature importance, both models",
         subtitle = "shares, since raw impurity is not on a common scale") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11)

  pg_clf <- cowplot::plot_grid(p_pp, p_imp, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 1.05))
  print(pg_clf)
  ggsave_if(here("plots", paste0("10_vs_classifier_", suffix, ".pdf")), pg_clf,
            width = 11, height = 4.8)
}
```

```{r fig_shap_compare, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.8}
# SHAP is computed in 11_shap_regression.Rmd, not here, so this reads its output if present. That
# keeps this notebook cheap: TreeSHAP on this forest takes far longer than fitting it.
shap_reg_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("shapreg_family_", suffix, ".csv"))
shap_clf_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("shap_family_", clf_suffix, ".csv"))
feat_reg_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("shapreg_feature_", suffix, ".csv"))
feat_clf_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("shap_feature_", clf_suffix, ".csv"))
have_shap <- all(file.exists(c(shap_reg_path, shap_clf_path, feat_reg_path, feat_clf_path)))

if (!have_shap) {
  cat("SHAP outputs not found. Run 11_shap_regression.Rmd (and 03_shap.Rmd for the classifier),\n")
  cat("then re-knit this notebook to fill in these panels.\n")
} else {
  fam_r <- read_csv(shap_reg_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::select(family, reg = share_pct)
  fam_c <- read_csv(shap_clf_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::select(family, clf = share_pct)
  fam_j <- inner_join(fam_c, fam_r, by = "family") %>% mutate(delta = reg - clf)

  p_fam <- fam_j %>%
    pivot_longer(c(clf, reg), names_to = "model", values_to = "share") %>%
    mutate(model = recode(model, clf = "classifier", reg = "regression"),
           family = fct_reorder(family, share, .fun = max)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(share, family, fill = model)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.65, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(classifier = "#0072B2", regression = "#E69F00"), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "share of total |SHAP| (%)", y = NULL,
         title = "(e) Family SHAP shares, both models",
         subtitle = sprintf("Spearman %.3f over %d families",
                            cor(fam_j$clf, fam_j$reg, method = "spearman"), nrow(fam_j))) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

  ft_r <- read_csv(feat_reg_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(reg = 100 * mean_abs_shap / sum(mean_abs_shap)) %>%
    dplyr::select(feature, family, reg, reg_cor = shap_value_cor)
  ft_c <- read_csv(feat_clf_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(clf = 100 * mean_abs_shap / sum(mean_abs_shap)) %>%
    dplyr::select(feature, clf, clf_cor = shap_value_cor)
  ft_j <- inner_join(ft_c, ft_r, by = "feature")

  p_ft <- ggplot(ft_j, aes(clf, reg)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
    geom_point(aes(colour = family), size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(guide = "none", end = 0.9) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = ft_j %>% filter(pmax(clf, reg) > 3 | abs(clf - reg) > 1.5),
      aes(label = feature), size = 2.5, max.overlaps = 18, seed = 9) +
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.5,
             label = sprintf("Spearman = %.3f\nn = %d features",
                             cor(ft_j$clf, ft_j$reg, method = "spearman"), nrow(ft_j))) +
    labs(x = "classifier SHAP share (%)", y = "regression SHAP share (%)",
         title = "(f) Feature SHAP shares",
         subtitle = "shares only: the two models' SHAP is in different units") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11)

  pg_shap <- cowplot::plot_grid(p_fam, p_ft, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 1.05))
  print(pg_shap)
  ggsave_if(here("plots", paste0("10_shap_vs_classifier_", suffix, ".pdf")), pg_shap,
            width = 11, height = 4.8)

  cat("\nFamilies where the two models differ most:\n")
  print(as.data.frame(fam_j %>% arrange(desc(abs(delta))) %>% head(6) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 2)))), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nWhether any of these clears replication noise is decided in 12_, not here.\n")
}
```

# Export

Writes the model, its importance, its metrics, its predictions, and the split itself.

**Decisions**

- Write nothing during a mutation run, so a deliberately corrupted run cannot be mistaken for a
  real result.
- Route every path through `assert_no_collision()`.
- Save the imputed and transformed split alongside the model, so `11_` explains this model's
  actual data instead of rebuilding it from parameters. The equivalent notebook in the frozen
  pipeline rebuilds it and then has to assert its way back to agreement.


```{r export, eval = !nzchar(params$mutate_target)}
# A mutation run never writes, so a corrupted matrix cannot be mistaken for a real result.
# Every path goes through assert_no_collision(), so no regression output can land on a
# classification filename and destroy a frozen baseline.
reg_save_rds(rf_model, file.path(out_dir, paste0("rfreg_model_", suffix, ".rds")))
reg_write_csv(importance_df, file.path(out_dir, paste0("rfreg_importance_", suffix, ".csv")))

perf <- bind_rows(
  metrics,
  if (isTRUE(params$run_cv)) tibble(
    metric = c("cv_spearman_mean", "cv_spearman_sd", "cv_pearson_mean", "cv_rmse_mean"),
    value  = c(mean(cv$spearman), sd(cv$spearman), mean(cv$pearson), mean(cv$rmse))) else NULL,
  # Written as a tribble so each metric NAME is bound to its value on the same row. The previous
  # two-parallel-vector form silently desynced - 10 names against 12 values - and the run failed
  # with "Tibble columns must have compatible sizes" rather than writing a wrong number, which
  # was lucky. A tribble cannot desync.
  #
  # Two AUCs, named for their comparator, because that is the whole difference between them.
  # Both define positives identically: outcome > the lfc cut AND padj < 0.05, on held-out genes.
  #   auc                     positives vs every OTHER held-out gene. Self-contained: needs no
  #                           external gene set, so it is comparable across knockdowns and
  #                           timepoints. This is the one reported.
  #   auc_vs_screened_ctrl    positives vs notebook 02's screened negative controls - genes
  #                           selected for having NO effect. That pool is not a neutral sample:
  #                           it is GC-enriched by +2.45 (Wilcoxon p = 2.7e-17), which inflates
  #                           the number (0.806 against 0.721 at si3d hypoxia 1hr). Kept only
  #                           for continuity with 02_; do not compare it across contrasts.
  if (isTRUE(params$auc_bridge)) tibble::tribble(
    ~metric,                    ~value,
    "auc",                       bridge$auc[2],
    "auc_ceiling",               bridge$ceiling[2],
    "auc_n_pos",                 bridge$n_pos[2],
    "auc_n_neg",                 bridge$n_neg[2],
    "auc_vs_screened_ctrl",      bridge$auc[1],
    "auc_vs_screened_ceiling",   bridge$ceiling[1],
    "auc_vs_screened_n_pos",     bridge$n_pos[1],
    "auc_vs_screened_n_neg",     bridge$n_neg[1],
    "matched_gene_auc",          matched_auc,
    "n_matched_genes",           as.numeric(n_matched)
  ) else NULL,
  if (exists("perm_metrics")) perm_metrics else NULL,
  tibble(metric = "split_seed", value = SPLIT_SEED),
  tibble(metric = "forest_seed", value = FOREST_SEED)
)
reg_write_csv(perf, file.path(out_dir, paste0("rfreg_performance_", suffix, ".csv")))

reg_write_csv(
  bind_rows(
    train_data %>% dplyr::select(gene_id_clean, symbol, y, y_padj) %>%
      mutate(pred = pred_tr, split = "train"),
    test_data %>% dplyr::select(gene_id_clean, symbol, y, y_padj) %>%
      mutate(pred = pred_t,  split = "test")),
  file.path(out_dir, paste0("rfreg_predictions_", suffix, ".csv")))

# The imputed, transformed split itself, so 11_shap_regression.Rmd explains this model's data
# rather than re-deriving it from params. 07c_ in the frozen pipeline re-derives and has to
# assert its way back to agreement; saving removes that whole class of drift.
if (isTRUE(params$save_model_data)) {
  reg_save_rds(list(train = train_data, test = test_data, feature_cols = feature_cols,
                    suffix = suffix, clf_suffix = clf_suffix,
                    target_transform = params$target_transform,
                    winsorize_y = params$winsorize_y, inv_scale = tf$inv_scale,
                    split_seed = SPLIT_SEED, forest_seed = FOREST_SEED),
               file.path(out_dir, paste0("rfreg_model_data_", suffix, ".rds")))
}
cat("Wrote outputs with suffix:", suffix, "\n")
```
